Every stocks market year gives you 2–3 real chances to make serious money.

You don’t decide when they come.
The market does.

That’s the part most traders never accept 👇

Most of the time, nothing works.

About 80% of stocks follow the general market:
- Trendless market → choppy, trendless stocks
- Strong uptrend → momentum everywhere
- Hard downtrend → shorting finally works

So the first question is never the stock.
It’s always the market.

Here’s how I think about it:

1) Trendless market = patience phase
If indices chop sideways for weeks or months, swing trading is hard.
You protect capital.
You trade less.
You wait.

Activity doesn’t equal progress.

2) Trending market = opportunity phase
When momentum is there, stocks behave cleanly.
Breakouts follow through.
Pullbacks work.
Holding gets easier.

That’s when you press.

3) Downtrend = different playbook
Strong downside momentum changes the rules.
Longs struggle.
Shorts finally offer clean moves.

Same logic. Different direction.

You don’t need fancy tools to see this.

Just look at the chart:
- NASDAQ above EMA8 + EMA21
- Higher highs, higher lows
- Clean structure, not noise

If that’s missing, stay out.

Yes, I use a more advanced trend model.
But even simple moving averages already do one thing perfectly:

They keep you from forcing trades
when the market isn’t paying.

Big money is made in short windows.
Not every week.
Not every month.

Your job isn’t to trade more.
Your job is to wait until conditions align.

That’s how you survive long enough
to be there when it finally matters.

📺 MEMORY STOCKS ARE NOT PARABOLIC LIKE $SLV & $GLD WERE

One of my core strategies – the 8-day moving average. When a stock is trading above both the 8/21-day moving averages, the bias should be long, and you stay with the sequence until it breaks.

This approach has been working particularly well in the memory names:

– $SNDK pulled back but never even touched the 21-day, reclaimed the 8-day, delivered strong follow-through. Trend remains clean and orderly, forming bull flags and building toward prior highs.

– $MU rebuilt above the 8-day while holding the 21-day, offered a small pullback entry around $455, now up roughly 11 points — solid continuation. Micron offers similar exposure as SanDisk with slightly smoother behavior.

– $WDC is a slower mover but technically constructive, entry around reclaiming the 8-day (~$254), potential add above $296, not overly extended.

This group has been moving together. If one leads, the others tend to follow.

Is this parabolic? Is a crash coming in memory stocks?

$SLV, for example, had a clear vertical acceleration phase and then snapped back hard. That’s classic blow-off behavior.

$SNDK and $MU, by contrast, advanced strongly, pulled back in a controlled way, reset near moving averages, and rebuilt technically. That’s constructive trend continuation — not exhaustion.

I believe that memory stocks are in the middle of a trend, not at the end. They are trending well, not going vertical.

Btw, I am still long a small $SLV position around $72.

📺 $IGV TACTICAL WIN, NOW A BIGGER QUESTION: IS SOFTWARE “DEAD”?

We had a great $IGV trade with the community, buying calls, trimming into strength, and fully exited on Tuesday — just before a downturn.

Now the focus shifts from “great trade” to structure: prior peak – $87.06, key pivot low – $81.93, key question – are we forming a W bottom or rolling over?

If price bounces but fails to reclaim higher levels → danger, if holds $81.93 and builds a higher low → possible rebuilding sequence, if breaks down without a meaningful bounce → stay cautious.

The bigger question: is software “dead”?

The Only EMA System You’ll Ever Need (Used the Right Way)

Price doesn’t “respect” indicators.
It respects the average cost of smart money.

That’s all EMAs are.

EMA = context, not magic.

• EMA 9 → Intraday traders
• EMA 21 → Swing traders
• EMA 50 → Trend traders
• EMA 200 → Investors & big trends

Different EMAs = different players.

Market control rule:
Price above EMA → Buyers in control
Price below EMA → Sellers in control

High-probability filter:
✔ Price above 200 EMA
✔ 21 EMA above 50 EMA
✔ Pullback toward 21 EMA
✔ Volume dries up on pullback
✔ Buy only on bullish candle near 21 EMA

Trend phases:
1️⃣ Initiation
2️⃣ EMA pullback
3️⃣ Momentum expansion
4️⃣ Weakness (stop chasing)

Exit like a pro:
• Take partials at 1:2 RR
• Move stop to breakeven
• Trail with 21 EMA
• Exit fully if price closes below 50 EMA

EMAs don’t predict.
They protect you from bad trades.

Trade with context. Stay patient.

Morgan Stanley Downgrades $DUOL to Equalweight from Overweight, Lowers PT to $100 from $245

Analyst comments: "With limited conviction the company can prove out the forward growth trajectory over the next few quarters. Our thesis had been that Duolingo would be able to drive user growth and monetization simultaneously. We were wrong and downgrade to Equalweight. As the company increased monetization over the course of 2025, the negative impact to user growth has been higher than we expected. We believe the likely culprit is reduced word-of-mouth marketing as increased monetization and messaging missteps weakened brand sentiment. To course correct, DUOL is making sizeable investments in the free user experience — increasing spend and reducing monetization.

The FY26 bookings guide of 10-12% y/y is ~3% below our forecast, while the EBITDA guide is -15% below, with margins set to contract -450 bps y/y as it makes Video Call more widely available. Although guidance had been highly conservative in the past, DUOL is now reducing that conservatism. The company expects these changes to stabilize DAU growth at ~20% y/y in 2026, but we'd note limited visibility given the number of planned changes."

– Can we hold yesterday’s lows and turn green for a tactical bounce?

It is frustrating, yes. But ranges eventually resolve. Until then, discipline and levels matter more than any predictions.
